To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Carmen Ruiz <carmen.ruiz@stratus.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 10 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Client continuity watchlist: Stratus AI QBR prep & exec attention

Team / Carmen —

Attaching a short watchlist for Stratus ahead of next week’s QBR. High level: usage dipped 18% month-over-month on the hosted API (mainly inference for internal search), procurement has paused the renewal until legal finishes the data processing addendum, and they flagged latency spikes on long chat sessions during the past month.

Key asks:
- Marissa: confirm renewal cadence and whether Sales can offer a 60-day pilot extension to smooth the conversation with procurement.
- Vivek: I need a 1‑pager (perf & mitigation) we can share with Carmen focusing on tail latency and recommended config changes (batching / kv-cache).
- Aditya: please surface any exec-side concessions (credit / SLA exceptions) we can consider — keep in mind we prefer technical remediation first.

Attached: stratus_watchlist.xlsx (watchlist + suggested actions), qbr_exec_brief.docx (one-page summary for execs).

Carmen — looping you in so we can align on what Stratus needs for the QBR. If there are new stakeholders on your side, please add them.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carmen Ruiz <carmen.ruiz@stratus.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Client continuity watchlist: Stratus AI QBR prep & exec attention

Kimberly — quick update from my side: procurement at Stratus escalated to a hold because of the DPA + retention language. I spoke to Carmen and confirmed they’re not canceling — they just need the legal team to sign off and a formal mutual action plan (MAP).

Proposed commercial play: 60‑day pilot extension with a usage credit of $8k to cover the month-over-month dip; we present this as a short runway vs an upfront discount. I can own the MAP doc and track signoffs.

If leadership is on board with the extension + credit, I’ll prepare the offer this afternoon and route for an exec approval chain. Otherwise we risk the procurement pause slipping into a full renewal delay.

—Marissa
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Carmen Ruiz <carmen.ruiz@stratus.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Client continuity watchlist: Stratus AI QBR prep & exec attention

Kimberly / Marissa / Carmen — attaching the technical note I promised (also saved to the Drive link). Highlights:
- Root cause: periodic KV cache thrashing on long chat sessions (seq len variance + high concurrency).
- Short-term mitigations (can be applied in <48 hrs): reduce max concurrency for long sessions, enable prefix caching for known conversational contexts, and temporarily increase batch window for background jobs.
- Medium-term: move Stratus workloads to a dedicated pool with a tuned quantization profile (saves ~22% tokens cost and reduces tail latency by ~120ms in tests).

If Carmen confirms, we can schedule a quick config change (30‑60 mins maintenance) that should reduce the reported spikes and buy us breathing room during procurement.

Vivek
Director, Reliability
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Carmen Ruiz <carmen.ruiz@stratus.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Client continuity watchlist: Stratus AI QBR prep & exec attention

Thanks — quick commercial note: leadership levers we can consider without escalating pricing broadly:
- One-time $8k usage credit (as Marissa suggested) conditional on MAP signoff within 14 days.
- SLA exception: offer a 99.5% latency SLO for the specific production route (requires limited-term runbook and post-mortem delivery).
- Fast-track legal review for the DPA amendment if Stratus commits to an executive sync this week.

If Kimberly wants, I can draft an approval memo for the execs (short, includes financial impact and risk score).

—Aditya (Sales Ops)
From: Carmen Ruiz <carmen.ruiz@stratus.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Client continuity watchlist: Stratus AI QBR prep & exec attention

Thanks, everyone — this is helpful and actionable. Quick responses:
- Procurement: we’ll prioritize the DPA review this week; I’ve added legal (samir.legal@stratus.ai) to the thread and requested a 48‑hour turnaround.
- The pilot extension + $8k credit is acceptable as a temporary measure while we complete legal — please send the MAP and credit terms.
- On the latency: we experienced the spike on Jul 3 during a data migration; a short config change to reduce concurrency for long sessions should be fine — schedule maintenance after 9pm PT and notify our ops channel.

Carmen
VP, Engineering — Stratus AI
